entries.example: A man from Njambo's Town had gone out to hunt, having with him bow and arrow, a machete, and a gun.
fields: 1) A machete is a large, broad knife used for cutting plants or other things.
In the story, a man carries a machete when he goes hunting.
A man from Njambo's Town had gone out to hunt, having with him bow and arrow, a machete, and a gun.
A machete is an object that can be counted; the word does not signal an operation.
1) The literati are people who are interested in literature or who know a lot about it.
The narrator calls a group the literati.
The word names a group; it does not give its size.

entries.example: Tortoise said, "Well! go! step aside from the path into the bushes, and we will wait for you here." But Civet said, "No! not in the bushes; for, I must go back to the kitchen-garden of my mother in our town." Tortoise exclaimed, "By no means!
fields: noun; used in the phrase «by no means»
1) A means is a way of doing something. 2) «By no means» means certainly not.
In the story, Tortoise exclaims «By no means!» to reject what Civet says.

Tortoise said, "Well! go! step aside from the path into the bushes, and we will wait for you here." But Civet said, "No! not in the bushes; for, I must go back to the kitchen-garden of my mother in our town." Tortoise exclaimed, "By no means!
In this phrase, «means» does not refer to an average or signal a calculation.
